items.markdown:
Collecting or identifying a **first edition Jane Austen** is a rare and prestigious milestone in the book world. During her lifetime, Austen published six major novels—all anonymously or credited simply as *"By a Lady"* or *"The Author of Sense and Sensibility."* 

### Austen’s Core First Editions (UK)

| Year | Title | Format | Original Publisher | Key Identification Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1811** | *Sense and Sensibility* | 3 Volumes | T. Egerton | Published on commission; title page reads "By a Lady"; issued in paper-covered boards with white spines. |
| **1813** | *Pride and Prejudice* | 3 Volumes | T. Egerton | Originally titled *First Impressions* ; published in Jan 1813; issued in 3 volumes anonymously. |
| **1814** | *Mansfield Park* | 3 Volumes | T. Egerton | Austen's first novel published on the standard risk/profit-sharing model rather than strictly on commission. |
| **1815** | *Emma* | 3 Volumes | John Murray | Dedicated by royal permission to the Prince Regent; published Dec 1815 (dated 1816 on title page). |
| **1818** | *Northanger Abbey* & *Persuasion* | 4 Volumes | John Murray | Published posthumously together as a 4-volume set; includes a "Biographical Notice of the Author" by Henry Austen revealing her identity for the first time. |

### Key Characteristics to Look For

- **The Anonymity Clue:** Genuine UK first editions of the first four novels will never bear the name "Jane Austen" on the title page.[[1]](https://janeaustens.house/object/sense-and-sensibility/)
- **Multi-Volume Sets:** Almost all of Austen’s first editions were issued in **duodecimo (12mo) or crown octavo in threes (3vols)** . Finding them complete with all half-titles and original boards is exceptionally rare.[[1]](https://janeaustens.house/object/sense-and-sensibility/)
- **Rebindings:** Because original paper boards were fragile, the vast majority of surviving 19th-century copies were rebound by contemporary owners in leather or half-calf.[[1]](https://janeaustens.house/object/sense-and-sensibility/)

### Where to Explore or Verify Copies

- **Museum Archives:** You can study authenticated copies and physical provenance details directly through the collection catalog at Jane Austen's House.[[1]](https://janeaustens.house/object/sense-and-sensibility/)
- **Rare Book Databases:** To track authenticated market availability, auction records, or appraise a physical copy, consult specialists via ABAQ (Antiquarian Booksellers' Association of America) or Biblio / AbeBooks.
